title: thin-slab defragmenter and coordinated spill controller to reduce KV cache fragmentation and IO spikes
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Production workloads with long-lived conversational sessions exposed two correlated issues: high KV cache fragmentation from many small allocations, and bursty spill IO when multiple tenants triggered background spill at similar times. This PR introduces a low-overhead "thin-slab" defragmenter plus a coordinated spill controller to address both problems without changing customer-visible cache semantics. Design summary: 1) Thin-slab defragmenter: lightweight compacting pass that bins tiny free regions and coalesces them into larger contiguous spans opportunistically during low-CPU windows. It operates per-tenant with a bounded work budget and uses lock-free handoffs to avoid pausing token-serving threads. 2) Spill coordinator: a central controller that sequences background spill and writeback jobs across tenants, enforces jitter windows, and exposes backpressure tokens to the allocator so that spill scheduling avoids IO storms. 3) Kernel scheduling hints: we add a small hint API used by the allocator to prefer contiguous page allocations for hot KV slices, improving prefetch locality on the most common model shard sizes. 4) Continuous batching compatibility: defragmenter avoids relocating active KV entries that are referenced by in-flight batch requests; we implemented epoch checks so batching threads are never interrupted. Implementation notes: - New modules: src/runtime/kv/defragmenter.rs, src/runtime/kv/spill_coordinator.rs, src/runtime/kv/alloc_hints.rs - Config knobs: defaults are conservative (defrag disabled by default per-tenant; coordinator enabled cluster-wide). Admin can flip via runtime config or Console. - Safety: defragmenter only moves cold or unreferenced entries; moves are tracked via a two-phase relocation with CAS semantics. - Telemetry: added metrics: kv.defrag.cycles, kv.defrag.reclaimed_bytes, kv.spill.coordinator.queue_depth, kv.spill.jitter_window_hits. Tests and benchmarks: - Unit tests covering relocation correctness and epoch safety. - Integration test driving high-fragmentation workload (simulated small allocations) and measuring spill behavior. - Microbenchmarks show: median token latency unchanged, p99 reduced by ~12% under heavy fragmentation workloads, memory reclaimed ~18% over 24h in synthetic tenant traces, spill IO spikes reduced (99th-percentile IO ops/sec down ~45%). Rollout plan: staged canary in dedicated region -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> full, with defrag off by default and coordinator on; we will enable per-tenant defrag gradually for tenants reporting fragmentation. Backout plan: coordinator can be disabled via feature flag; defrag toggles per-tenant and per-instance. Risks & mitigations: - Reclamation could interact with paging on overloaded hosts; we added spill backpressure and an emergency throttle to stop defrag if IO latency exceeds threshold. - Edge case: relocation races with external snapshotting; added compatibility hook for snapshot to pause defrag. Documentation: added docs/kv/cache-defrag.md and Console rollout UI docs. Related: builds on design discussions in ENG-4821 and incident SUP-902.

release_notes: Add thin-slab defragmenter to reclaim small fragmented KV regions and coordinated spill controller to sequence background spill jobs and reduce IO spikes. Default configuration is conservative: coordinator enabled cluster-wide; per-tenant defrag is opt-in. Improves tail latency and reduces spill bursts under highly fragmented workloads.
notes_for_ops: Canary rollout started in region us-west-2. Ops should watch metrics kv.defrag.reclaimed_bytes, kv.spill.coordinator.queue_depth and IO latency. To disable coordinator set helm kv.coordinator.enabled=false or flip runtime flag; defrag can be toggled per-tenant via admin API.
risk_assessment: Medium: introduces background relocation work and cross-tenant coordination. Mitigations: conservative defaults, IO backpressure, emergency throttle, snapshot pause hook.
